In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dsRNA and RV16-induced overproduction of TLR3 and RIG-I-like cytokines (TNF-α, CXCL8, and IFNβ) is exaggerated in COPD-BECS.
dsRNA- and rhinovirus-induced overproduction of Tslp in COPD epithelial cells is mediated by endosomal TLRs.
dsRNA and RV16 induce TSLP production in COPD-BE via endosomal TLR 3, whereas dsRNA-LyoVEC induces TSLP production via RIG-I-like receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

viral infection and viral-like stimulation of bronchial epithelium in chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder (COPD), via endosomal toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3), induces an exaggerated release of the TH2-switching cytokine thymic stromolymphopoietin (TLSP).
TLR3 is involved in the overproduction of TLP in COPD-BECS and that this is a potential therapeutic target for future studies.
RV16 and ds RNA-induced epithelial TLP overproduction in COPD is mediated by endosomal TLR 3, but not by cytosolic RLG-I like helicases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
viral infection and viral stimuli induce exaggerated cytokine responses in the airway epithelium of COPD.
the overproduction of TLR3-induced cytokines by COPD-BEC, in particular TSLP, may play a role in the TH2-like inflammation that is characteristic of COPD exacerbations and the development of COPD.
the epithelial TSLPs production is enhanced by viral stimuli, in particular by dsRNA, which is a viral component and is a TLR3 agonist, and by RV16, a rhinovirus.
